subject: Embeddings pipeline: private peering + SDK auth next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Park <erin@datasurge.com>, platform-ops@datasurge.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings pipeline: private peering + SDK auth next steps

Hi Erin — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end so your platform team can scope internal work: 

1) Goal recap
- Datasurge wants an embeddings + reranker pipeline that does inference against a private Redwood model endpoint (low latency, no public egress).
- Requirements highlighted: VPC peering / private endpoint, IP allowlist for management APIs, mTLS for SDK traffic, DNS resolution inside VPC, and structured output for downstream tool-calls.

2) Proposed technical approach
- Private VPC Endpoint (Redwood-managed ENI) in your account using AWS PrivateLink or equivalent; no public NAT for inference traffic.
- SDK auth: short-lived client certificates issued via your CA or our integration with your KMS (we sent a sample flow attached).
- Routing: Route inference flows via the private endpoint; control-plane calls (billing/usage) can be whitelisted to specific management IPs if needed.
- Embeddings + rerank: We’ll expose a embeddings-only model variant for batch/async embeddings and a low-latency reranker model for rerank calls; both reachable via the same private endpoint.

3) Immediate asks for Datasurge ops
- Share a network diagram showing the VPC where the endpoint should live (attach below).
- Confirm whether you prefer PrivateLink (endpoint service in Redwood account) or an AWS VPC peering approach — both work, tradeoffs noted inline.
- Provide a point person for mTLS cert rotation and an initial list of IPs/subnets to allow.

4) Next steps / timeline
- If we get the diagram and choice of endpoint by EOD Thu (16 May), our infra team can draft the infra template and a playbook within 3 business days.
- Marissa will follow up on SDK integration examples and a structured-output schema for your tool-calling use case.

Attachments: network-diagram.png (requested areas highlighted), redwood-sdk-auth-sample.zip (sample cert handshake + SDK snippet)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the infra template.

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Erin Park <erin@datasurge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@datasurge.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings pipeline: private peering + SDK auth next steps

Jordan — appreciated the clarity. Quick answers inline: 

- We prefer PrivateLink (simpler for our security team) unless you identify a perf blocker.
- Attached is a high-level network diagram from our infra team. The VPC we’d like to use is vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2).
- For mTLS cert rotation: looping in platform-ops (platform-ops@datasurge.com) — they own cert lifecycle.

Questions from my side:
- Do you support routing inference traffic through our IGW for logging, or does PrivateLink bypass that? We need to keep egress logs for audit.
- For embeddings throughput, any recommended batching settings you want us to benchmark as part of the pilot?

We can target the 16 May decision point.

Thanks,
Erin Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Datasurge
erin@datasurge.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: platform-ops@datasurge.com, Erin Park <erin@datasurge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings pipeline: private peering + SDK auth next steps

Hi Erin / Platform Ops — jumping in with the engineering handoff and a few pragmatic notes from our end. 

1) PrivateLink + logging
- PrivateLink traffic does not traverse your IGW by default. If you need VPC-native egress logging (flow logs) we recommend deploying a flow-collector in the same VPC and mirroring logs there; alternatively we can configure our endpoint service to emit connection logs to a customer-dedicated CloudWatch log group (requires IAM cross-account role). We can include steps in the infra template.

2) mTLS and SDK auth
- Two supported options: (A) Customer-managed certs (you provision a trust bundle, you rotate; we validate client certs on our side), or (B) Short-lived certs issued by Redwood with provisioning via your KMS; option B reduces operational lift for your ops team. Both support auto-rotation hooks in the SDK.
- For initial integration, option B is fastest — Marissa can share a sample rotation flow (attached in the SDK sample zip).

3) Batching/throughput guidance for embeddings
- Start with continuous-batching enabled, target 16–32 tokens per request and 8–16 concurrent inflight requests for the pilot. We’ll adjust during load testing. We’ll provide a small Jupyter notebook to run microbenchmarks.

4) Reranker pattern
- Best practice: surface embeddings as dense vectors from the embeddings endpoint, then call the reranker endpoint with a short context plus top-K candidates. We’ll provide a small reference rerank wrapper in the sample repo.

5) Action items (owners)
- Erin / platform-ops: confirm PrivateLink and share IAM role / contact for cross-account logging (due: 16 May).
- Datasurge infra: confirm VPC subnet IDs for the endpoint (due: 16 May).
- Marissa: share SDK snippets, structured-output schema, and rerank wrapper (due: 17 May).
- Jordan: prepare infra template + PrivateLink instructions (due: 18 May).

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: platform-ops@datasurge.com <platform-ops@datasurge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings pipeline: private peering + SDK auth next steps

Thanks everyone — we confirmed PrivateLink is the preferred approach and we can create the cross-account IAM role next week. Answers below and a couple of notes:

- VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2) — subnets: subnet-0aa111, subnet-0bb222 (private).
- Logging: we’ll accept a cross-account role for Redwood to deliver connection logs to our CloudWatch group; please include the IAM trust policy example.
- mTLS: we prefer option A (customer-managed certs) to align with our internal compliance policy; we’ll provide a trust bundle and rotation cadence (quarterly) — pending Jordan’s infra template.
- Rerank: we’ll start with top-10 candidate ranking; will evaluate top-50 in perf tests.

Attachment: datasurge-network-diagram-v2.pdf (high-level) — referenced as network-diagram.png in earlier thread.

Actionables confirmed: PrivateLink + customer-managed certs + cross-account logging role. Please send infra template and SDK snippets and we’ll schedule a 60-minute joint runbook session next Wed (23 May) to walk through deployment.

Regards,
Datasurge Platform Team
platform-ops@datasurge.com
